limitations: Desktop headless Chromium, DPR 1; viewport emulation is not a physical phone.
Geometry/texture counters are shared renderer totals, grouped by visible UI/world phase; they are not per-scene asset ownership.
WebGL live counters mean create minus explicit delete calls, not allocated bytes or GPU memory; GC/context loss may retire native objects independently.
CPU render submission excludes GPU completion. Automation transition time includes input transport and two-frame settling.
Heap is JavaScript memory, not GPU memory; post-GC checkpoints intentionally run outside transition timing.
Instrumentation and automation add overhead. A short run cannot establish absence of leaks.
Firefox executable probe is not a browser compatibility test.
